newsitem.title: USA: Teco to merge with Lykes Energy.
newsitem.headline: Teco to merge with Lykes Energy.

text.p: Teco Energy Inc said it agreed to merge with Lykes Energy Inc in a stock-for-stock deal valued at $300 million.
Teco said it expects the deal to initially be slightly dilutive to earnings, but sees favorable future growth prospects.
The companies expect some cost savings and efficiencies gained by cutting duplicative overhead and administrative activities, as well as improved operating efficiencies and lower interest costs.
Lykes Energy owns Peoples Gas System Inc, a regulated, retail gas distributor in Florida; Peoples Gas Company, a propane business; and a unit involved in natural gas marketing.

"At the gas company, we already had begun a productivity review and restructuring which could result in changes in job responsibility and possible reductions in the workforce," said John Brabson, Lykes Energy's president.

"That process is intended to allow us to become more competitive and to continue to grow our company. It is not anticipated that the merger itself will lead to any major layoffs or downsizing," Brabson said.
In the proposed deal, Lykes Energy shareholders will receive shares of TECO Energy common stock for shares of Lykes Energy common stock they currently hold.
The number of TECO shares to be issued will depend on the average market price during a specified period prior to the closing, subject to a collar.
Based on Teco's closing price Thursday of $24.75, the number of shares would be about 12.1 million.

This merger, to be accounted for as a pooling of interest, has been approved by both companies' boards of directors. The deal, which is expected to close in mid-1997, remains subject to certain shareholder and regulatory approvals.
Teco said it's quarterly dividend of $0.28 a share remains in effect and will not be affected by the transaction.
